lead.headline: Trump says 'one or two' Iran targets remain as Tehran floats Hormuz plan
lead.dek: Khamenei warns of no geographic limits if war resumes; Qatar says an LNG carrier was hit Friday in the Gulf
body: President Donald Trump said Saturday the United States still has to "take care of" one or two targets in Iran, including a suspected underground nuclear site, as Iran's foreign minister said a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days was under discussion with Qatari mediators and an Iranian delegation held talks in Doha.

Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned Saturday there would be no geographical limits on Iranian attacks if the war resumed, Iranian state media said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no decision had been made on new strikes and that talks "have actually never stopped." U.S. Central Command said its blockade has redirected 144 vessels.

The U.S. and Israel began striking Iran Feb. 28; a ceasefire was reached in April, and a June 18 memorandum on Hormuz navigation stalled. Qatar Gas Transport said the LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by "unidentified objects" Friday with no injuries. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran sees no need to meet U.S. officials until its conditions, including oil waivers, are met.

briefs.headline: Virginia and D.C. sue to block Trump's 250-foot arch
briefs.summary: The attorneys general filed a 45-page suit Saturday calling the Memorial Circle project unlawful; the administration plans to begin construction Nov. 5.

briefs.headline: Alaska asks judge to toss DOJ suit over Senate ballots
briefs.summary: The Republican-run state said Saturday the demand to set aside votes for a second Dan Sullivan is "meritless" and impossible under ballot secrecy, three days before Election Day.

briefs.headline: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3B Binance theft
briefs.summary: The bureau said Saturday the TraderTraitor unit is converting the funds to ether. Binance said it has replaced 90% of the stolen assets and will reopen withdrawals Sunday.

briefs.headline: Mamdani says Trump will grant visa to slain Bronx boy's mother
briefs.summary: The New York mayor said after a call Saturday that the mother of Javits Frimpong, 15, shot on his way to school Thursday, will get a visa immediately. No arrests have been made.

briefs.headline: Taiwan says Chinese patrol is harassing shipping off east coast
briefs.summary: Taiwan's coast guard said late Saturday that two Chinese coast guard ships were broadcasting 'law enforcement' radio messages in its eastern exclusive economic zone and sent its own vessels to monitor them.

briefs.headline: Police fire tear gas as 320,000 march across France
briefs.summary: Mostly young marchers protested the cost of living and school conditions for a third straight Saturday; the interior ministry counted 320,000, with 70,000 in Paris, and at least 290 arrests. Organizers put turnout near 500,000.

briefs.headline: Russia reports 'massive' drone attack on Kstovo industrial site
briefs.summary: Gov. Gleb Nikitin said more than 100 drones were downed overnight and a Kstovsky district facility took 'significant damage.' Kyiv Post, citing OSINT monitors, reported the target was Lukoil's Kstovo refinery.

briefs.headline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as Nigeria probes 2 suspected cases
briefs.summary: Health ministry data Saturday showed 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections in the Bundibugyo outbreak declared in May, the second-deadliest on record. Nigeria's disease agency isolated two suspected cases in the northeast pending lab tests.

briefs.headline: PSC closes five days of MARL hearings, ruling due by March
briefs.summary: The Public Service Commission wrapped up five days of testimony Friday on NextEra's 100-plus-mile Mid-Atlantic Resiliency Link, with more than 190 landowners as interveners. The PSC has said it will rule on certification by March 2027.

briefs.headline: Early voting closes with turnout 30% ahead of 2022 pace
briefs.summary: In-person early voting ran through 5 p.m. Saturday. More than 115,000 absentee and early ballots had been cast through Wednesday, about 30% more than the same point in the 2022 midterm, Secretary of State Kris Warner's office said Friday.

briefs.headline: Morrisey-linked PAC sent Senate mailers to wrong districts
briefs.summary: Black Bear PAC spent nearly $20,000 Oct. 26 on mailers backing Sens. Anne Charnock and Laura Chapman that landed in each other's districts, West Virginia Watch reported Saturday, citing a Secretary of State filing.

briefs.headline: State sends $3.9M to CAMC for rural health workforce programs
briefs.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey announced three Rural Health Transformation awards Friday: $500,000 for rural clinical training, $1.69 million for Kanawha County provider fellowships and $1.74 million to keep chronically ill workers employed.

regional.item: The Marshall Marathon closes its downtown, riverfront and Ritter Park route from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. today, with towing on posted blocks.
Kanawha County Schools asks voters Tuesday to renew the excess levy that funds 22% of its budget, this time through 2034.
Jurors in Gregory Casto's trial for the 2014 death of Cindy Ball heard closing arguments Friday and begin deliberating Monday.

away.item: Village trustees filled three Water Board seats Oct. 21, two left by resignations; the board meets Wednesday.

hotspots.item: Webster Springs' town council, sitting as Addison, approved an ordinance recognizing the town's original 1892 charter Oct. 13, The Webster Echo reported.
North Topsail Beach aldermen hold a public hearing Wednesday at 11 a.m. on new parking definitions and penalties in the town's public safety code.

briefs.headline: Cougars blow 4-1 lead, lose fifth straight in Wenatchee shootout
briefs.summary: Prince George fell 5-4 to the Wild on Friday after leading 4-1 in the third, its third blown third-period lead of the skid. The club added defenceman Jace McFaul from Swift Current and visits the Giants in Langley today.

briefs.headline: Prince George Hospice's first 50/50 pays out $223,375
briefs.summary: The Hospice and Palliative Care Society drew the winner Friday and said the proceeds go to its grief counselling service. Its Dream Home Lottery draw is Feb. 26.

briefs.headline: B.C. keeps its clocks as the U.S. and eastern Canada fall back
briefs.summary: From today most of the province sits at UTC-7 year-round, one hour ahead of Washington state and two behind Ontario. Vancouver's latest winter sunrise will be 9:08 a.m., the first winter without a change in more than 100 years.

briefs.headline: Poilievre asks Carney to drop diesel taxes before Thursday's budget
briefs.summary: In a letter ahead of the Nov. 5 budget, the Conservative leader wants all federal diesel taxes gone until Canada Day and the GST off fuel until summer. The budget office projects a $63.3B deficit for 2026-27.

briefs.headline: Elections Alberta says 2027 vote may need old map or a delay
briefs.summary: Chief electoral officer Gordon McClure told the Speaker on Friday the Oct. 18, 2027, vote should run on current boundaries or be postponed; a vote takes up to 18 months to prepare. The new riding map is tabled Monday.

briefs.headline: CHAPEA crew exits NASA's Mars habitat after 378 days
briefs.summary: Four volunteers walked out of the 1,700-square-foot 3D-printed habitat at Johnson Space Center on Saturday, a year and 12 days after entering. NASA said two weeks of post-mission evaluations follow.

briefs.headline: Seabirds jet-lag themselves and veer off course, Oxford GPS data show
briefs.summary: A Science study of 335 Manx shearwater homing flights found the birds' sun compass slips four minutes per degree of longitude crossed, bending their course by up to 15 degrees.

briefs.headline: NASA asks industry for ideas to reboost or service Hubble
briefs.summary: An Oct. 29 request for information seeks ways to raise the telescope's orbit, service it or guide a controlled reentry by 2032. Responses are due Nov. 30; NASA predicts reentry in 2033 or 2034 without a boost.

briefs.headline: IEEE retracts 1,417 conference papers in a single day
briefs.summary: Nature's analysis found the Oct. 23 batch, the largest bulk retraction on record, matches papers a study traced to paper-mill ads selling authorship for $43 to $400. IEEE said the papers "may have been offered for sale."

briefs.headline: Judge lets NAACP Clean Air Act suit against xAI proceed
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Debra Brown denied xAI's motion to dismiss claims that it ran at least 35 gas turbines at its Colossus data center outside Memphis without air permits, ruling the turbines are not "mobile sources."

briefs.headline: Backdoored Anthropic extension sat in Cursor marketplace 11 hours
briefs.summary: Cursor said a tampered Claude Code extension reached up to 5,000 users Thursday and tried to install an SSH backdoor. Researchers told Ars it shipped through Anthropic's official account; neither company has said how.

weather_ear: Sunday's forecast, from Jim Claudtore, lands at 7:15.
kicker: The clocks went back overnight; Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line, and the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, seven days out.
